_doc: Framework default controls, their sinks, and their documented bypasses
Read `escapes_by_default` carefully: it is NOT true for every framework.
Jinja2 autoescaping is off unless configured, and JSP `<%= %>` is raw. A
control may therefore never be credited merely because a framework is present -
crediting is per framework AND configuration.
A control is credited only when it covers the finding's weakness class, sits on
the traced path to the sink, has no bypass on that path, and every file on that
path was parsed. Anything less is 'unassessed', which caps confidence and never

controls.residual_impact: The sanitizer strips script elements, event-handler attributes and javascript: URLs, but permits anchors, images and formatting. Content and layout spoofing remain achievable; script execution does not.
JSX escapes interpolated text and attribute values. Markup injection is not achievable through ordinary interpolation.
Mustache interpolation, v-bind and v-text escape HTML. Injection requires an explicit raw-HTML directive.
Template autoescaping is on by default and escapes interpolated values.

frameworks.name: Jinja2
frameworks.escape_default_note: Autoescaping is OFF unless the environment sets autoescape=True or select_autoescape(...). Presence of Jinja2 is therefore NOT evidence of a control; the environment configuration must be found before anything is credited.

controls.residual_impact: When explicitly enabled, autoescaping escapes interpolated values.
th:text and [[...]] inlining escape their values.

frameworks.name: JSP / JSTL
frameworks.escape_default_note: Scriptlet expressions `<%= %>` and bare EL `${...}` are raw. Only <c:out> escapes, and only while escapeXml is not false. A JSP page is not escape-by-default.

controls.residual_impact: <c:out> escapes XML entities in the value it renders.
Contextual auto-escaping applies per output context (HTML, attribute, JS, CSS, URL).
